High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 Bench At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Parties through their counsel.

The present appeal is filed under Section 71 (6) of Foods Safety and Standard Act, 2006 against the order dated 03.09.2014,
by which the Appellate Authority, Mandleshwar has dismissed the appeal as time barred.
 There is an order dated 08.05.2012 passed by adjudicatory Authority/Additional Collector, Khargone under the provisions of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 against the present appellant,
by which he has been punished under Section 26 (2)(II) read with Section 52 (2) of the Act of, 2006 with the fine of Rs.1,00,000/-.
 Initially the appellant filed a writ petition bearing WP No.5498/2012 against aforesaid order before this Court.
During pendency of that writ petition, the District and Sessions Judge has been designated as Appellate Authority under the Act of 2006.

By order dated 14.02.2014, the writ petition was disposed of with the direction to the appellant to avail the alternate remedy available under the law by filing appeal within the period of 6 weeks from the date of order.

After the aforesaid, the appellant preferred an appeal before the District and Sessions Judge, Mandleshwar along with the application under Section 5 of Limitation Act for seeking condonation of 22 days delay in filing the appeal.
The said application came up for consideration before the Appellate Authority on 03.09.2014.

The Appellate Authority did not any find valid explanation for condoning the delay hence accordingly rejected the application under Section 5 of Limitation  HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  BENCH AT INDORE  MA No.2161/2014 Act and dismissed the appeal also.
Hence the present appeal before this Court.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is a businessman and he was not aware that who has been designated as Appellate Authority.
He conducted an inquiry and then came to know that District and Sessions Judge has been appointed as Appellate Authority and because of which the appeal could not be filed within 6 weeks.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the arguments raised by the learned counsel for the appellant.

On 14.02.2014, the Government Advocate has informed this Court in WP No.5498/2012 that the Authority has been notified but did not disclosed that which authority has been notified as appellate authority and this court disposed of the writ petition by direction the appellant to approach the appellate authority.
Thereafter appellant has inquired about name of the appellate authority and due to which delay has been occurred.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Esha Bhattacharejee Vs Managing Committee of Raghunathpur Nafar Academy and Other reported in (2013) 12 SCC 649 has held thus:-
"The Principles applicable to an application for condonation of delay are as follows:-
i) There should be a liberal, pragmatic, justice-oriented, non- pedantic approach while dealing with an application for condonation of delay, for the courts are not supposed to legalise injustice but are obliged to remove injustice.

entities.text: Esha Bhattacharejee Vs Managing Committee of Raghunathpur Nafar Academy and Other reported in (2013) 12 SCC 649
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
ii) The terms "sufficient cause" should be understood in their proper spirit,
philosophy and purpose regard being had to the fact that these terms are basically elastic and are to be applied in proper perspective to the obtaining fact- situation.
HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH BENCH AT INDORE iii) Substantial justice being paramount and pivotal the technical considerations should not be given undue and uncalled for emphasis.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH BENCH AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: iv) No presumption can be attached to deliberate causation of delay but, gross negligence on the part of the counsel or litigant is to be taken note of.
v) Lack of bona fides imputable to a party seeking condonation of delay is a significant and relevant fact.

vi) It is to be kept in mind that adherence to strict proof should not affect public justice and cause public mischief because the courts are required to be vigilant so that in the ultimate eventuate there is no real failure of justice."
Thus, because of the limitation, the party should not be left remedyless even otherwise there is a delay of only 17 days in approaching the appellate authority.
Keeping in view the reasons mentioned in the appeal, the delay is liable to be condoned.
The appellate authority is directed to decide the appeal on merits.
The matter is remitted back.
